title: Zero-touch VPC onboarding lifecycle and offline compatibility acceptance criteria
creator: Avery Chen
description: Define and validate requirements for a zero-touch VPC onboarding lifecycle that supports fully offline (air-gapped) sites, minimal operator intervention, and deterministic rollback during upgrades. Outcome: a clear acceptance criteria checklist for engineering and solutions that enables self-serve setup for network teams with strict egress restrictions.
background: Customers deploying Redwood Private in isolated VPCs ask for a frictionless onboarding flow that can run without internet egress or with tightly controlled egress windows. Today onboarding requires manual operator steps, custom operator manifests, and ad-hoc artifact transfer for air-gapped installs. This PRD captures requirements and acceptance criteria to move toward zero-touch and repeatable offline-compatible onboarding.
goals: Document a deterministic onboarding sequence that can be executed with zero interactive operator commands for standard VPC templates.
Support two onboarding modes: online (limited egress) and air-gapped (no egress).
Provide manifest and artifact packaging conventions for unattended bootstrap (signed bundles).
Define rollback and upgrade-safe checkpoints so operators can abort without manual cleanups.
non_goals: Automating custom network topology mapping for non-standard on-prem routers.
Replacing customer CI/CD or existing operator tooling (we provide operator hooks, not full orchestration).
Building a universal provisioning tool for every cloud provider—we standardize on documented templates first.
requirements: R1: Onboarding bundle format - a signed tarball (SHA256 + signature) containing control-plane images, operator manifests, and an onboarding plan (YAML) describing steps and timeouts.
R2: Deterministic plan execution - the operator must run the onboarding plan idempotently and emit a machine-readable execution log with step timestamps and outcomes.
R3: Offline artifact staging - provide an 'airgap mirror' utility that creates and validates the signed bundle from Redwood's artifact registry for a specific release tag.

R4: Minimal required outbound - for limited-egress installs, we support a single whitelisted endpoint for artifact provenance checks and timestamp validation; all other artifacts are pulled from the staged bundle.
R5: Safe checkpoints - onboarding includes at least three rollback checkpoints (pre-pull, post-control-plane, post-data-plane) with automated rollback hooks.

R6: Telemetry and audit - when egress is allowed, a lightweight attest-only heartbeat can be optionally sent; for air-gapped installs all logs remain local and a standardized export bundle is produced for support.
R7: Operator UX - the CLI for 'zero-touch-run' accepts only the signed bundle and a minimal config (CIDR, KMS key id), validates preconditions, and returns non-zero codes for fatal checks.
R8: RBAC & KMS integration - onboarding must surface required KMS key provisioning steps in the plan and verify key existence without transmitting keys externally.
R9: Documentation - deliver runbook templates for both online and air-gapped modes with troubleshooting sections and exact network rules required.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Given a standard VPC template and a signed onboarding bundle, running the operator in 'airgap' mode completes the control-plane and worker provisioning end-to-end within the documented timeout without requiring any additional operator commands.

AC-2: Deterministic execution logs are generated and include step id, start/finish timestamps, stdout/stderr capture, and artifact checksums. Logs must be parseable by the Console's offline import tool.

AC-3: The airgap mirror utility can produce a signed bundle for any supported release tag; validating the bundle verifies all image digests and manifest signatures locally (no external network calls).

AC-4: Rollback checkpoints are exercised in a chaos test: when a simulated failure occurs at the 'post-control-plane' step, the operator performs the documented rollback actions and leaves the cluster in a recoverable state with no orphaned CRs or dangling storage attachments.
AC-5: For limited-egress installs, the operator makes at most one TLS call to an allowlist domain for attest/provenance; all other content is sourced locally from the bundle.

AC-6: The onboarding CLI returns standardized exit codes and writes a final 'onboard-result.json' bundle describing final state, IPs, and next steps. Engineering verifies parsing with the console import flow.
AC-7: Security review signoff completed and security checklist items (KMS usage, signature verification, least-privilege RBAC) are marked as done by security engineering.
rollout_notes: Phase 1: internal alpha with Solutions Eng and 2 pilot customers (one online-limited egress, one fully air-gapped). Phase 2: broader beta with template library for AWS, Azure, GCP VPCs. Phase 3: GA when acceptance criteria met and 3 pilot customers have completed successful installs.
migration_impact: Existing customers using manual onboarding will retain support for the legacy flow for at least two releases. Migration guides and converter tools will be provided to generate signed bundles from current operator artifacts.
risks: RISK-1: Bundle signing complexity could cause key management confusion for customers; mitigated by detailed KMS runbooks and sample scripts.
RISK-2: Offline checksum mismatches due to image mutation during mirroring; mitigated by strict release immutability and mirror validation tests.
RISK-3: Customers with bespoke network topologies may still require bespoke operator intervention; mitigated by templating and an escalation matrix to Solutions Eng.
open_questions: Q1: What is the minimum set of control-plane services that must be present in the bundle for a minimal viable air-gapped install? (engineering input required)
Q2: Should the signed bundle include pre-baked cloud-init scripts for node bootstrapping or leave node bootstrap to customer tooling?
Q3: How do we surface and test KMS integration in fully offline environments where HSM/KMS is hosted in a separate VPC with limited peering?
notes: This ticket focuses on the onboarding lifecycle and acceptance criteria; separate tickets will cover operator refactors and console integration for import parsing. Ensure coordination with ENG-17340 (artifact signing) and SECURITY-42 (KMS patterns).
